questions.question: How can Citizenship be offered and accepted during play, and what may or must be exchanged?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Grand Scepter holder (not taken this turn) offers any Exile including self exactly one Reliquary relic plus optional binding exchange favor,secrets,banners,non-Reliquary relics. Accepted: flip Citizen, replace all board/map warbands purple as available with recipient choosing shortfall removals/replacements, discard revealed Vision, Usurper→Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, refresh full. Exchange agreed items; Chancellor gains uncovered mandatory modifier. All Imperials rule purple sites. Reliquary relics inaccessible to Campaign/Recover, powers unusable, do not count goals.
questions.observed_answer:
**Offer:** the Grand Scepter cannot make an offer on the turn its current holder took it. In later turns it may offer any Exile, including itself. Must promise **exactly one Reliquary relic**; may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners and non-Reliquary relics. May let recipient peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics.

**Acceptance:** flip to Citizen; replace all own warbands on board/map with purple. If insufficient purple, new Citizen chooses which to remove and which to replace. Discard revealed Vision, flip own Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered **mandatory** Reliquary modifier. **Forced Citizenship** powers apply the same status-conversion steps without a negotiated offer: no required Scepter offer or Reliquary relic gift, and no invented promised exchange. Only an actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier. All Imperials rule purple sites; Citizenship does not itself grant a separate shared victory.

If winner Exile, flip **all** Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile must do both: **flip their board to Citizen** and **replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site**, regardless of the old garrison size. questions.question: In later-game setup with five players, how much favor goes in each bank, what is on the banners, and what resources and warbands start on each kind of player board?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: Four favor per suit bank (three with two–four players). People’s Favor normal with one favor, Darkest Secret one secret. 2. Collect shared pieces and both banners. People's Favor begins normal side with 1 favor; Darkest Secret has 1 secret. Put **3 favor per suit bank**, or **4 each with 5–6 players**.

questions.observed_answer:
Use packets A, B and C and the Playbook's setup, preferably with four players. Choose a Chancellor and seat them on the short edge by the Cradle; seat Red, then Blue, then Yellow clockwise from the Chancellor. Do not shuffle the prepared first-game decks. The packet-based one-round walkthrough is optional teaching guidance; play afterwards uses the full rules here.

1. Lay out the map. Put Plains faceup in top Cradle slot, Mountain faceup in top Provinces slot, Rocky Coast faceup in top Hinterland slot.
